desc:
An array is fair if the sum of its elements at even positions (0, 2, 4, ...) equals the sum of its elements at odd positions (1, 3, 5, ...).

Count the indices i such that removing nums[i] leaves a fair array. After a removal, all later elements shift one position to the left, so their parity of position flips. Each index is tested independently on the original array. An array with a single element left (position 0, no odd elements) is fair only if that element is 0; an empty array is fair.

nums = [2, 1, 6, 4]
remove index 0 -> [1, 6, 4]: even 5, odd 6
remove index 1 -> [2, 6, 4]: even 6, odd 6  fair
remove index 2 -> [2, 1, 4]: even 6, odd 1
remove index 3 -> [2, 1, 6]: even 8, odd 1
answer = 1
hints: Simulating each removal and re-summing is O(n) per index, O(n2) in total. What part of the array keeps its parities after removing index i?
Elements before i keep their positions. Elements after i all move one place left, so even-position elements there become odd-position ones and vice versa.

Prefix sums of even-position and odd-position elements give the sums before i; the matching suffix sums come from the totals. New even sum = even before i + odd after i, new odd sum = odd before i + even after i.
editorial: Let E and O be the sums of the original even- and odd-position elements. While scanning, keep pe and po: the even- and odd-position sums strictly before the current index. The sums strictly after index i are then E - pe - (nums[i] if i is even) for even positions and O - po - (nums[i] if i is odd) for odd positions; call them se and so.

After removing index i the elements before it are unchanged, and those after it swap parity. The array is fair exactly when pe + so == po + se. Count the indices for which this holds. One pass with O(1) extra state gives O(n) time and O(1) space. The empty and single-element cases fall out of the same formula.
